turns.user: I use a 30-minute ticket and change from metro M2 to metro M3.
turns.agent:
Yes—a 30-minute mobile ticket covers a transfer from M2 to M3, since transfers between metro lines are allowed without the usual extra transfer validation. Keep within the ticket’s 30-minute transfer window; if your final transfer happens before it expires, you can finish that last ride after the window ends.

That’s according to the 5 November 2026 snapshot; it describes mobile tickets, which require an internet-connected phone and have no paper equivalent. See BKK’s 30-minute ticket rules. I can’t verify current rules live, so check BKK’s page before travelling.

turns.user: After that I board tram 4. Do I need to validate again?
turns.agent:
Yes—activate or scan the 30-minute mobile ticket again when you board tram 4. The snapshot says to validate at the start of a journey and when changing to another line; the exception is transfers between metro lines, so it doesn’t cover the change from M3 to a tram. The tram transfer must also fall within the 30-minute window. If it is your final transfer and happens before the window ends, you may finish that tram ride after expiry.

This is based on the 5 November 2026 snapshot. See BKK’s 30-minute ticket rules. I can’t verify current rules live, so check BKK’s page before travelling.
